Put the operations skills together into the shape of a real continuous-integration
step: a **clean, consistently-formatted** suite tree, run **in parallel**,
producing **one report**. That is what a green pipeline looks like.

You have already met the pieces — Robocop to format, Pabot to parallelise, one
`output.xml` to report on. Now assemble them.

## Task 1 — Make it clean

Format the messy suite so the whole tree is consistent:

```bash
uv run robocop format checks/unformatted.robot
```

**Check:** `checks/unformatted.robot` is consistently formatted.

## Task 2 — Run it like CI

Run all the clean suites in parallel, into a single report:

```bash
uv run pabot --outputdir results checks/alpha.robot checks/beta.robot checks/unformatted.robot
```

Every suite runs at once, into one green report:

```terminal
$ uv run pabot --outputdir results checks/alpha.robot checks/beta.robot checks/unformatted.robot
[0] EXECUTING Alpha
[1] EXECUTING Beta
[2] EXECUTING Unformatted
[0] PASSED Alpha in 0.5 seconds
[1] PASSED Beta in 0.5 seconds
[2] PASSED Unformatted in 0.4 seconds
5 tests, 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
```

Every test from every suite runs concurrently and lands in one
`results/output.xml` — formatted, fast, and green. Wire exactly this command into
a CI job and you have a working pipeline step.

**Check:** the parallel run passes with every test — the operations tier complete.
